requirements.title: DEALLOCATE deallocates allocatable variables and pointer targets
requirements.definition: Execution of a DEALLOCATE statement deallocates the listed allocatable variables. When a listed allocate-object is a pointer, execution deallocates the pointer target and causes the listed pointer to become disassociated; the requirements that make an allocatable variable or pointer target eligible for deallocation are owned by 9.7.3.2 and 9.7.3.3, and the STAT-determined status after an error is owned by 9.7.4.

pending.allocatable-variable-deallocated: PENDING complete source allocating an allocatable INTEGER object, defining a literal before DEALLOCATE, executing DEALLOCATE with STAT=, and after STAT=0 using only the permitted ALLOCATED inquiry to observe unallocated status plus an independent sentinel. The plan does not reference the allocatable value, bounds, or storage after deallocation.
pending.pointer-target-deallocated: PENDING complete source allocating a data pointer target with ALLOCATE, defining a literal before DEALLOCATE, executing DEALLOCATE(p, STAT=s), and after s==0 using only ASSOCIATED(p)=.FALSE. for the listed pointer and a separate sentinel. The pointer target is not dereferenced after deallocation.
pending.listed-pointer-disassociated: PENDING complete source with a pointer allocated by ALLOCATE and known associated before DEALLOCATE, then after successful deallocation observing the listed pointer's disassociated status by ASSOCIATED. Non-vacuousness comes from a pre-deallocation literal assignment and post-deallocation status inquiry only.

requirements.title: A DEALLOCATE statement has a parenthesized allocate-object list and optional deallocation options
requirements.definition: The grammar for deallocate-stmt is exactly DEALLOCATE ( allocate-object-list [ , dealloc-opt-list ] ). R944 owns the DEALLOCATE keyword, parentheses, required nonempty allocate-object-list, and optional comma-introduced dealloc-opt-list; it does not by itself decide whether a particular allocate-object is an allocatable variable or eligible pointer target.

pending.deallocate-keyword: PENDING diagnostic/control source contrasting DEALLOCATE(x) with a misspelled keyword in an otherwise valid program where x is an allocated allocatable variable. The repaired control uses STAT=0 and only ALLOCATED inquiry after deallocation; invalidity is attributable to R944 keyword syntax.
pending.parenthesized-allocate-object-list: PENDING positive-control source using DEALLOCATE(x) for one allocated allocatable variable, observing STAT=0 in a variant with STAT= and an independent sentinel. The object-list form is material because no dealloc options are present.
pending.optional-dealloc-opt-list: PENDING positive-control source using DEALLOCATE(x, STAT=s, ERRMSG=msg) with x allocated beforehand, observing s==0 and an independent sentinel after the permitted ALLOCATED inquiry. STAT= and ERRMSG= meanings remain 9.7.4 and 9.7.5 dependencies.
pending.missing-object-list-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source attempting DEALLOCATE() with no allocate-object, repaired by adding a single allocated allocatable variable. The invalidity is attributable to R944's required allocate-object-list, not to C957 or 9.7.3.2 status rules.
pending.malformed-parentheses-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source omitting one required parenthesis around an otherwise valid allocate-object list, repaired by adding only that parenthesis. The repaired control reaches STAT=0 and no value of a deallocated object is read.

requirements.title: A deallocation option is STAT= or ERRMSG=
requirements.definition: The grammar for dealloc-opt admits exactly STAT=stat-variable or ERRMSG=errmsg-variable. R945 admits these keyword forms; the scalar integer stat-variable rule and STAT values are owned by 9.7.4, and the errmsg-variable requirements and message assignment are owned by 9.7.5.

pending.stat-dealloc-option: PENDING positive-control source DEALLOCATE(x, STAT=s) where x is allocated before the statement; after successful execution observe s==0 through 9.7.4 and an independent sentinel. The plan does not induce a deallocation error.
pending.errmsg-dealloc-option: PENDING positive-control source DEALLOCATE(x, STAT=s, ERRMSG=msg) with x allocated before the statement; after s==0 observe only that normal control reaches a literal sentinel and, through 9.7.5, no failure-message content is used as an oracle.

requirements.title: No deallocation option appears more than once in a given dealloc-opt-list
requirements.definition: For a given R945 dealloc-opt-list, no dealloc-opt shall appear more than once. Thus at most one STAT= option and at most one ERRMSG= option may occur in the same DEALLOCATE statement; distinct STAT= and ERRMSG= options may appear together subject to 9.7.4 and 9.7.5.

pending.distinct-options-control: PENDING positive-control source DEALLOCATE(x, STAT=s, ERRMSG=msg) with x allocated beforehand, observing successful STAT=0 and an independent sentinel. This controls C957 by using two distinct options rather than duplicate options.
pending.duplicate-stat-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source DEALLOCATE(x, STAT=s1, STAT=s2) with x otherwise an allocated allocatable variable and both stat variables otherwise valid. Repair only by deleting one STAT= option and observe successful deallocation; invalidity is attributable to C957, not R945 or 9.7.4.
pending.duplicate-errmsg-rejected: PENDING diagnostic/control source DEALLOCATE(x, ERRMSG=m1, ERRMSG=m2, STAT=s) with both errmsg variables otherwise valid. Repair only by deleting one ERRMSG= option and observe successful deallocation; invalidity is attributable to C957, not R945 or 9.7.5.

requirements.title: Allocate objects in the same DEALLOCATE statement are independent of each other and options
requirements.definition: Within a single DEALLOCATE statement, an allocate-object shall not depend on the value, bounds, allocation status, or association status of another allocate-object in that same statement. It also shall not depend on the value of the stat-variable or errmsg-variable in that statement. This is a program restriction, not a mandatory static diagnostic for every execution-time status dependency.

pending.no-value-dependence: PENDING diagnostic/control source where one allocate-object designator uses the value of another allocate-object in the same DEALLOCATE statement, with both objects otherwise valid and allocated. Repair by saving the selector value in an independent scalar before DEALLOCATE or by splitting statements; invalidity is attributable to S9.7.3.1-002.
pending.no-bounds-dependence: PENDING diagnostic/control source where one allocate-object designator uses LBOUND/UBOUND/SIZE of another allocate-object listed in the same DEALLOCATE statement. Repair by computing the bound before the statement or using independent bounds; the repaired oracle is successful deallocation and independent sentinels only.
pending.no-allocation-status-dependence: PENDING diagnostic/control source where an allocate-object selection depends on ALLOCATED of another allocate-object in the same DEALLOCATE statement. Repair by capturing the inquiry result before the statement; attribution excludes 9.7.3.2 unallocated-deallocation errors by ensuring the control objects are allocated.
pending.no-association-status-dependence: PENDING diagnostic/control source where one pointer allocate-object selection depends on ASSOCIATED status of another pointer allocate-object in the same DEALLOCATE statement. Repair by using a status value captured before the statement; no undefined pointer status is queried.
pending.no-stat-or-errmsg-value-dependence: PENDING diagnostic/control source where an allocate-object subscript or component selection depends on the value of the STAT= or ERRMSG= variable appearing in the same DEALLOCATE statement. Repair by using an independent scalar or character length set before the statement; invalidity is attributable to S9.7.3.1-002, not to R944/R945 option spelling.

requirements.title: DEALLOCATE error conditions are processor dependent and no-STAT errors terminate
requirements.definition: The set of error conditions for a DEALLOCATE statement is processor dependent. If an error condition occurs during execution of a DEALLOCATE statement that has no STAT= specifier, error termination is initiated. Detailed STAT= and ERRMSG= behavior is owned by 9.7.4 and 9.7.5.

pending.processor-dependent-error-set-boundary: PENDING source-only classification plan listing standard-specified deallocation error conditions from 9.7.3.2, 9.7.3.3, and 9.7.4 as portable facets while leaving processor-dependent extensions untested. Future executable cases must use 9.7.4 STAT observations or the no-STAT termination rule and must not deliberately cause resource exhaustion or rely on compiler agreement.
pending.error-without-stat-initiates-error-termi: PENDING non-resource source plan using a standard deallocation error without STAT=, such as attempting to deallocate an unallocated allocatable variable in an otherwise valid program. The repaired control adds STAT= or allocates first and reaches a literal sentinel; attribution is to S9.7.3.1-003 plus the underlying 9.7.3.2/9.7.3.3 error condition, not syntax.

requirements.title: Multiple successful deallocations occur in processor-dependent order
requirements.definition: When execution of one DEALLOCATE statement deallocates more than one allocated object, the order of those deallocations is processor dependent. Portable tests cannot require one order unless another subclause imposes an ordering such as finalization or coarray synchronization.

pending.multiple-object-order-processor-dependen: PENDING source-only classification plan with two independently allocated objects in one DEALLOCATE statement, recording that future executable tests may observe only final statuses or independent sentinels and must not require either deallocation order. If finalizers are used, expected finalizer order remains processor dependent unless constrained by 7.5.6.
